 5   REPLY BRIEF OF ROBERT FREEHILL, PRO SE INTERVENOR, REGARDING THE
 6                   REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13
 7

 8   To the Honorable Administrative Law Judges:

 9   Robert Freehill, a pro se intervenor respectfully files this Reply Brief to the Administrative Law

10   Judges pursuant to SOAH Order No. 35. As such, this brief replies to the Applicants’ arguments

11   on remanded Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13.

12      I.      INTRODUCTION

13   In the Proposal for Decision (PFD) issued on 20AUG26, the Administrative Law Judges

14   recommend “that Oncor and LCRA's applications for the proposed Bell County East-to-Big Hill

15   Project and the Big Hill-to-Sand Lake Project (the Applications; the Projects) be denied.” The

16   Administrative Law Judges must reaffirm this recommendation; that the applications for the

17   Projects be denied.

                                                                           Reply Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                         SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                            Page 1 of 7
  1   “Everyone who listens to these words of mine and acts on them will be
 2   like the wise man who built his house on rock. The rain fell, and the
 3    floods came, and the winds blew and buffeted the house. But it did
 4      not collapse; it had been set solidly on rock. And everyone who
 5   listens to these words of mine but does not act on them will be like a
 6   fool who built his house on sand. The rain fell, and the floods came,
 7    and the winds blew and buffeted the house. And it collapsed and was
 8                    completely ruined.” Matthew 7:24-27
 9

10   The reaffirmation of a recommendation for denial is reinforced by a review of the remanded

11   issues 11 and 13:

12             Preliminary Order Issue 11. Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet

13   state or federal reliability standards?

14             Preliminary Order Issue 13. What is the estimated congestion cost savings for

15   consumers that may result from the proposed transmission facilities considering both current and

16   future expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce

17   those congestion levels?

18

19       II.      STATEMENT OF POSITION

20   The Applicants have not established that the that the Projects are necessary for the service,

21   accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public under Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA

22   § 37.056); nor, that congestion cost savings to consumers is provided, to the consumer, in the

23   application. SOAH Order No. 35 keeps the evidentiary record closed and requires pinpoint

24   record citations.1

25




     1 SOAH Order No. 35 at 2-3 (Sept. 22,2026), Docket No. 59475, Item 6597.

                                                                            Reply Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                 PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                          SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                             Page 2 of 7
  1   A-Preliminary Order Issue 11: Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet

 2   state or federal reliability standards?

 3

 4   PURA § 37.056(a) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b), certification requires a finding of

 5   necessity for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public. When evaluating

 6   reliability for a proposed project in the ERCOT region, this requires consideration of forecasted

 7   load supported by quantifiable evidence and any review conducted by ERCOT must incorporate

 8   the historical load, forecasted load growth, and additional load currently seeking interconnection.

 9   The forecasted load growth and additional load currently seeking interconnection must be

10   substantiated by quantifiable evidence of projected load growth.2 Furthermore, PURA §

11   37.056(c)(1)-(2) requires consideration of existing service and the need for

12   additional service; subsection (c-1) addresses historical load, forecasted growth, and loads

13   seeking interconnection in reliability evaluations.3

14

15   According to the record, HB5066 and the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP) are the

16   foundations of Applicants' assertion of need for the Bell County East-to-Big Hill and Big Hill-to-

17   Sand Lake Projects.4 There are significant load forecast and planning discrepancies in the

18   record. The original PBRP's extra-high-voltage analysis was focused on 2038 and the record

19   contains contrary evidence concerning the timing of Import Path 2, including ERCOT's

20   December 12, 2024 sequencing letter prioritizing two other import paths for 2030.5 Further in



     2 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii)(II).
     3 PFD at 55-57; Act of May 25, 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., ch. 892 (H.B. 5066), § 1
     4 PFD SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475 pg 53
     5 Applicant Exhibit JG-2, pg 8

                                                                                Reply Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                     PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                              SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                                 Page 3 of 7
  1   JG-2, pg 8, the applicants cite that “ERCOT will be evaluating the EHV needs for 2030 as a part

 2   of its 2024 RTP.” This must be reconciled. If the PBRP is the foundation of need for the

 3   Projects, the relationship of the 2024 RTP to it must be comprehended.

 4

 5   The PFD also identifies, correctly, that the S&P Global Study which underpinned the PBRP’s

 6   load projections, was overstated and outdated.6

 7

 8   Complicating this is the missing codification of Central Texas’ power generation capabilities.

 9   Applicants present that “…Import paths are those transmission projects needed to transfer power

10   from other regions into the Permian Basin region to serve the projected demand.”7 Yet, The

11   PBRP does not identify the amount of available generation capacity that will exist at the time

12   these forecasted loads are to materialize.8 The full scope of the power environment must be

13   understood for the determination of solutions for transmission line courses of action.

14

15   B- Preliminary Order Issue 13: What is the estimated congestion cost savings for

16   consumers that may result from the proposed transmission facilities considering both

17   current and future expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission

18   facilities to reduce those congestion levels?

19




     6 PFD SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475, pg 178, item 108
     7 App. Ex. 1 (Application), att. 5 (PBRP) at Bates 1877.
     8 PFD SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475, pg 62.

                                                                           Reply Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                         SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                            Page 4 of 7
  1   The Applicants did not submit the information called for by the cost issues-neither the estimated

 2   cost of the facilities to consumers nor the estimated congestion cost savings to consumers.9

 3

 4   C-Applicant’s Directory: Intervenor Mark Allen Bradbury’s coverage of the Applicant’s

 5   Directory is concise and to the point, I adopt his verbiage.10

 6

 7      III.      FINDINGS

 8   I respectfully request that the subsequent PFD find:

 9      •      the record does not establish that Bell County East-to-Big Hill Project and the Big Hill-

10             to-Sand Lake Project facilities, considered as the facilities before the Commission in this

11             CCN, are necessary to meet a specified state or federal reliability standard; and

12      •      the record does not establish a quantified estimate of consumer congestion cost savings

13             attributable to these proposed facilities;

14   Upon confirming these findings, the Applicants have not established that the requested CCN is

15   necessary. There is no project-specific reliability showing under Issue 11 and the total absence

16   of a project-specific consumer congestion-savings estimate under Issue 13 confirm the ALJ’s

17   original recommendation.

18

19      IV.        CONCLUSION AND PRAYER




     9 PFD SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475, pg 149
     10 MARK ALLAN BRADBURY'S REPLY BRIEF REGARDING

     REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13, pg 5.
                                                                              Reply Brief of Robert Freehill
                                                                                   PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                               Page 5 of 7
  1   The Commission remanded this case because Issues 11 and 13 required answers. Based on the

 2   closed record, the answers are clear. Applicants did not prove that these particular facilities are

 3   necessary to meet a specified state or federal reliability standard, and they did not prove the

 4   amount of consumer congestion cost savings attributable to these facilities.

 5

 6   I, Robert Freehill, pro se Intervenor respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges

 7   reaffirm the original recommendation: that the Public Utility Commission of Texas DENY the

 8   application for a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity in PUC Docket No. 59475.

 9
